components.text: Restoration is a benefit that can replenish all or part of the available sum insured after a policy-defined trigger. Its practical purpose is to make additional cover available again according to the product's restoration rules after earlier use of cover.
components.boundary: Restoration is not automatically present in every policy and does not guarantee payment of a later claim.

components.text: The restoration trigger is the condition that causes restored cover to become available. Products can define that trigger differently, including how much prior cover must have been used and when restoration becomes available.
components.boundary: Do not assume restoration happens after any use, only after full exhaustion, or at any other universal trigger without the applicable product rule.

components.text: Restoration mechanics can vary in how much cover is restored and how many restorations are available in a policy period. A product may define a restoration percentage, restoration count, timing rule and utilization sequence.
components.boundary: Do not assume a full fresh sum insured, unlimited restorations, or immediate reuse unless the product terms say so.

components.text: Whether restored cover can be used by the same insured person, for the same illness, in the same hospitalization or only in a later hospitalization can be controlled by separate restoration conditions.
components.boundary: Same-person, same-illness and hospitalization reuse are product-specific; do not treat them as universally allowed or prohibited.

components.text: In a family-floater policy, restoration can interact with the shared pool of available cover. Whether restored cover becomes available to other members, the member who made the earlier claim, or both depends on the product's floater and restoration rules.
components.boundary: Do not guarantee that every family member receives a fresh amount after one member uses the shared cover.

components.text: When comparing restoration benefits, useful dimensions include the trigger, amount restored, number of restorations, timing, same-illness and same-person rules, covered scope, utilization sequence and floater operation.
components.boundary: This checklist explains what to compare; it does not rank or recommend a policy.

customer_document_boundary: Customer-specific sum insured, prior claims in the policy period, covered members, selected options, endorsements, and applicable policy dates must be verified before applying a restoration rule to that customer.
definition: Restoration of sum insured is a product benefit that replenishes all or part of the available sum insured after a governed trigger, subject to product-specific conditions and limits.

examples.scenario: A policyholder has already used part of the available health cover and the policy includes a restoration benefit.
examples.result: If the product's stated restoration trigger and conditions are satisfied, the available cover may be replenished according to that product's restoration rule.
examples.boundary: This example does not establish when restoration triggers, how much is restored, whether it can be used for the same illness or hospitalization, or whether a particular claim will be paid.

limitations: This record explains the generic restoration concept only.
Restoration is not automatically available in every health policy and is not automatically triggered after every claim.
The amount restored, number of restorations, trigger, timing, usage sequence, same-illness rules, and member or floater operation are product-specific.
It does not determine claim admissibility, approval, payment, entitlement, or recommendation.
plain_language_explanation: Restoration is a feature that can refill all or part of your available sum insured after a policy-defined trigger. Think of it as the policy making additional cover available again, but only according to the restoration rules written into that product.
practical_implication: The important question is not simply whether a policy has restoration, but how that restoration works. Different products can differ on when it activates, how much comes back, how many times it can happen, and when the restored amount can be used.
product_specific_boundary: Restoration percentage, trigger requirement, timing, number of restorations, same-hospitalization or subsequent-hospitalization use, same-illness rules, covered scope, utilization sequence, policy-year reset, carry-over, and floater operation must come from governed product knowledge.
